dailyRead: The day turns on one Sunday interview rather than on anything that happened in the Gulf. Treasury Secretary Bessent told Face the Nation that the Fed may be making a policy mistake if it overtightens, pointing at hawkish remarks from governors and at months of tightening financial conditions, and he pushed back on the fifty-point December move Governor Waller had floated. The repricing that followed is specific and worth reading carefully: NQ is 3.0% higher at 25,882, YM is 1.46% higher at 48,919, and gold is about 2% higher at 3,618 - equities and gold up together, on the same news, is a terminal-rate story and not a risk-sentiment story. December itself has barely moved, still roughly 90% on Kalshi to 96% on FedWatch for a quarter point on December 9; what moved is everything after it, which is why the most rate-sensitive index got paid first and the price-weighted Dow lagged. That ordering is the trade. The dollar is softer against seven of eight, DXY 103.674 and minus 0.13%, and the two havens are giving back only a fraction of Friday - USD/JPY 158.942 and plus 0.25%, USD/CHF 0.83934 and minus 0.06%. The yen lost to all seven others, but it did so with Tokyo shut for Labour Thanksgiving, so treat 158.942 as holiday liquidity rather than a change of view: the December 18 hike to 1.50% is still expected by 86% of economists and the Ministry of Finance sits immediately above at 160. The franc held better than the yen and now leads the board on its own, because the SNB has no policy story at 0.00% and the Gulf is a direct input. And the Gulf keeps escalating without being paid: UKMTO reported another tanker on fire in the engine room early Monday, the sixth hit since Sunday, after two separate projectile strikes near Khasab on Saturday and an incident involving military forces in the Gulf of Oman, and the IRGC claimed attacks on Bahrain - yet WTI is 83.52 against the 83.98 Friday settle and Brent 92.63 against 92.57. Three weekends running, the premium has refused to be paid, which keeps the Canadian dollar at minus one and keeps the Bank of Canada disagreement with TradingEconomics alive into Macklem on Tuesday at 19:25. The cleanest expressions today are the ones where both legs still point the same way after the bounce: long the euro and sterling against the Australian dollar into Wednesday CPI, and long gold now that Friday forced selling has visibly ended. The cleanest mistake would be to add to the crowded Australian and Canadian shorts into Wednesday at 02:30 and 15:30 - this is the week where a squeeze is cheaper for the market than a trend. Flash PMIs at 10:15, 10:30, 11:30 and 16:45 are the live risk to the whole construction, because the US prints are forecast to decelerate hard, to 54.5 manufacturing from 56.0 and 55.6 services from 57.9, and growth doubt would undercut exactly the trade Bessent words started.

USD.when: December 9 at 21:00 with a new dot plot, and the fifty-point tail now pushed back by the Treasury itself
USD.note: TradingEconomics carries the Fed funds rate at 4.00% as the upper bound of the 3.75% to 4.00% range, held on October 28, and its own quarter-end projection is 4.25%. The quarter point is still near-certain - about 90% on Kalshi, 95.7% on a November 19 FedWatch reading and 96.9% in later coverage - but the new input is political rather than monetary: Treasury Secretary Bessent said on Sunday that the Fed may be making a policy mistake if it overtightens, citing hawkish governor remarks and a substantial tightening in financial conditions, and pushed back on the fifty-point move Waller had floated. That caps the path beyond December rather than December itself, which is exactly how gold and NQ can rally together. The October 28 minutes record that almost all participants judged further action to raise the target range would likely be appropriate and that a couple would consider more than 25 basis points on unfavourable inflation data, so core PCE on Wednesday at 15:30 is what decides whether the tail returns - November CPI only lands on December 10, after the meeting. New York Fed President Williams, who has said the situation does not call for dramatic action, speaks Monday at 23:00. The meeting carries a Summary of Economic Projections, so the dot plot is the larger half of the event.

EUR.note: TradingEconomics carries the deposit facility rate at 2.50%, with the main refinancing rate at 2.65% and the marginal lending rate at 2.90%, all held on October 29 - Lagarde confirmed at that press conference that a hike was discussed but the hold was unanimous. Euro-area inflation is 4.0%, a three-year high, with core at 2.6% and rising, and the energy input behind that print is still live: EU natural gas now reads 92.89 euros against the 88.45 the last report carried, on the Troll field outage and lower Norwegian exports, with storage 69.8% full on November 19 against 81.2% a year earlier. Pricing is a near-certain quarter point without being a formality: ECB Watch at 92.0% and LSEG around 91% on November 18, against roughly 72% in mid-November after Nagel warning and about 84% at the October meeting. Today the flash PMIs are the live test - French services forecast at 47.4 from 48.4 and German services at 52.4 from 51.7 at 10:15 and 10:30, which is the same two-speed euro area the Council keeps describing. The October accounts arrive Thursday at 14:30, Nagel speaks Friday at 14:40, and French and Spanish November flash CPI on Friday give the first read on euro-area November inflation. Lagarde steps down on February 7, 2027.

GBP.when: December 17 at 14:00, the most two-sided decision on this board at 78% to 84% against an economist consensus to hold
GBP.note: TradingEconomics carries Bank Rate at 4.00% after the November 5 quarter-point rise from 3.75%. The vote was nine of nine to hike with Catherine Mann wanting fifty basis points to 4.25%, and the Bank said inflation is expected to rise to around 5% by the middle of next year before falling back, with recent activity data stronger than expected. CPI is 3.6% with core steady at 2.8% and unemployment improved to 4.6%, though the ONS has flagged Labour Force Survey sample rotation and wage growth has slowed to 3.6% from 3.8%. The split is genuine: market pricing sits between 78% and 84% - RateProbability at 78% on November 20, Blue Gamma at 84% on November 18 - while all but one of 65 economists polled by Reuters expect a hold, with February the consensus for the next move. The market side has names on it, which is what changed this month: Chief Economist Huw Pill has signalled rates likely rising again in December and through 2027, and Deputy Governor Lombardelli will not rule out voting for one. Pill speaks today at 15:00 and Greene on Tuesday at 14:30, with the flash PMIs at 11:30 forecast at 53.0 manufacturing and 53.0 services. TradingEconomics own quarter-end projection is still 4.00%, so it reads this as a hold.

JPY.when: December 18 at 05:00, forecast at 1.50% with 86% of economists agreeing - but a two-sided event
JPY.note: TradingEconomics carries the policy rate at 1.25% after the October 30 hold, an 8-1 vote with Hajime Takata dissenting for faster hikes toward neutral, and its calendar forecasts 1.50% for December 18. A Reuters poll of 71 economists run November 11 to 18 has 86% expecting that quarter point, which would make this the first three-hike year in 37 years, and nearly 60% expect 1.75% by the end of March. October national core CPI was 2.2% against a 2.3% forecast, so it missed, but core has been above the 2% target for a second straight month and headline is 2.3%. Wage growth is 4.6%, the fastest on this board, and unemployment is 2.4%. The carry gap is unchanged on TradingEconomics at 2.16 points, the US 10-year at 4.944% against the Japanese 10-year at 2.785%, with cash Treasuries not yet repriced for Sunday news. The important nuance is that December is not one-way: Bank staff put the nominal neutral rate anywhere between 1.1% and 2.5% with no board consensus, the hike is largely priced, and several analysts warn a vague statement or cautious Ueda press conference risks a repeat of last December hike-and-sell. Spot at 158.942 keeps the Ministry of Finance the nearer risk, with intervention having capped the pair around 160 before. Tokyo core CPI arrives Friday at 01:30 forecast at 2.9% from 2.6%, and Tokyo is closed today for Labour Thanksgiving.

AUD.when: December 8 at 05:30, with TradingEconomics carrying 4.85% and the hurdle for more now visibly higher
AUD.note: TradingEconomics carries the cash rate at 4.85% after the November 3 rise from 4.60%, an 18-year high, and forecasts a hold for December 8. The November minutes are the key detail: six of nine members supported that rise, citing inflation above target, resilient activity and the possibility that a higher neutral rate had made policy less restrictive than assumed, while three opposed it, warning that rising unemployment and falling house prices could push the economy into a sharper downturn. TradingEconomics own summary reads that split as a higher hurdle for further increases, with markets increasingly expecting the peak. The board is stuck: it cannot hike into October unemployment at a four-year high of 4.9% after employment fell 43,500 against a forecast of plus 25,500, and it cannot cut into headline inflation at 4.3% with core at 3.6%, the highest on this board. October CPI on Wednesday at 02:30 is the only release that can move this, and the ForexFactory consensus reads headline 4.8% from 4.3%, monthly 0.4% from 0.8% and trimmed mean monthly steady at 0.3% - energy pass-through lifting the headline while the targeted core measure does not accelerate, which argues the freeze holds even on a hot headline. A market that already expects 4.8% and gets it is how the most crowded short on this board gets squeezed, and this morning that squeeze has started.

NZD.when: December 9 at 03:00, where TradingEconomics forecasts 3.00% from 2.75%
NZD.note: TradingEconomics carries the Official Cash Rate at 2.75% after the October 28 hold - which undershot both the 3.0% consensus and TradingEconomics own 3.0% forecast - and forecasts 3.00% for the December 9 Monetary Policy Statement. This remains the only move outside the Fed, ECB and Bank of Japan that this board carries. The Reserve Bank November Survey of Expectations supports it: respondents expect the cash rate to reach 3.05% by the end of the December quarter and 3.40% over the next year, up from 3.21% in the previous survey, with one-year inflation expectations rising to 2.92% from 2.60% and two-year to 2.36% from 2.34%. Against that, Q3 CPI fell to 3.7% from 4.1% with core steady at 3.2%, unemployment rose to 5.7%, the highest since 2016, employment fell 0.1% on the quarter and private wage growth is 2.0%. Quarterly retail sales landed overnight at 23:45 forecast at 0.5% from minus 0.5% with the core measure at 0.8%, a low-impact release and not one the Worker has posted an actual for yet. The kiwi is the laggard of this bounce, up only 0.10% against the dollar, which says the policy leg is doing the work and the price leg is not.

CAD.when: December 9 at 16:45, with TradingEconomics forecasting 2.75% against a rate market near 38%
CAD.note: TradingEconomics carries the overnight rate at 2.50% after the October 28 rise from 2.25%, the first increase in three years, and forecasts 2.75% for December 9. The Bank said the move aimed to reduce the risk that continuing high energy prices spread to other goods and services, noted there could be a need to raise further although caution is necessary, and projected CPI averaging 3% in 2027 before returning to 2% in mid-2028, with growth of 1% in 2026 and 2% in each of the next two years. The problem is that the energy pass-through it was aimed at keeps going in reverse: six tankers have now been hit in the Gulf since Sunday and WTI still reads 83.52 against the 83.98 Friday settle, with the barrel 14% lower on the month. Meanwhile core CPI is 2.0%, trimmed 1.8% and median 2.0%, all at or below the midpoint, headline held at 3.1%, unemployment is 6.7% and employment has fallen three months running. That leaves a real disagreement rather than a rounding error between the TradingEconomics forecast and a rate market near 38%. Governor Macklem speaks Tuesday at 19:25 and is the single best chance of resolving it before December 9.

CHF.when: December 10 at 10:30, with TradingEconomics carrying 0.00% and no case for anything else
CHF.note: TradingEconomics carries the SNB policy rate at 0.00%, held on September 24 and held there since mid-2025, and forecasts 0.00% for December 10. At the September meeting the bank said the current stance remains appropriate, noted inflation had risen on higher energy prices, and forecast average inflation of 0.7% in 2026 and 0.8% in both 2027 and 2028, with GDP growth of 1.5% to 2% in 2026 and around 1.5% in 2027, flagging high uncertainty from Middle East tensions, global growth, trade policy and exchange rates. Crucially it repeated that it remains willing to intervene in foreign exchange markets as necessary. October headline inflation is 1.5%, near a three-year high, but core is 0.5% and the gap between them is imported energy rather than domestic pressure, so there is no policy story here at all. That is precisely why the franc led the board this morning: with no rate expectation to unwind, it held Friday haven bid better than the yen did and beat it by 0.31% on the cross. The cap is intervention rather than policy, and UBS economic expectations on Wednesday at 11:00 are the only domestic item this week.

geopolitics: Day 268 of a closed Strait of Hormuz, and the weekend escalated further without moving the price of oil. UKMTO reported that a tanker transiting outbound through the strait was struck by an unidentified projectile about 11 nautical miles north of Khasab on Saturday and a second was hit in its engine room 17 nautical miles east of Khasab, both without casualties, one of them running with its identification and navigation systems switched off in defiance of issued warnings. On Sunday UKMTO reported a tanker involved in an incident with military forces in the Gulf of Oman near Chabahar, close to the American blockade line, while Iranian state media quoting the navy said two supertankers caught fire after striking mines in a restricted area east of the strait - the same pattern of competing and unverifiable accounts as the previous weekend. Early on Monday UKMTO reported another attack inside the strait that left a fire in the engine room, which the IRGC said it carried out at around 08:00 Bucharest and which Iranian claims make the sixth tanker hit since Sunday. The IRGC also claimed attacks on Bahrain, which Manama said its air defences defeated and which it says targeted a facility; the IRGC described the targets as US Patriot sites. Iran demands are unchanged and explicit: an end to the war on all fronts, unfrozen assets, oil sanctions lifted and the American counter-blockade of Iranian ports ended, and the foreign minister has told the Qatari mediator that discussing the reopening of the strait is pointless until they are met. The FX read is the important part, and it is the same read for the third weekend running: a direct military exchange, six commercial vessels hit in three days and an attack on a Gulf state produced WTI at 83.52 against the 83.98 Friday settle and Brent at 92.63 against 92.57. The market is pricing an IEA surplus near 2 million barrels a day, a US-China-Russia agreement to lift refined output and American statements that flows through the strait are at record levels, and it is pricing those ahead of the headlines. That keeps the Canadian dollar at minus one, because the energy pass-through the Bank of Canada hiked for in October is the one input that keeps reversing, and it keeps the franc at plus two rather than higher, because a haven bid that oil will not confirm is a shallow one. The asymmetry is now very large: what turns this into a crude long and a Canadian dollar long overnight is a supply response that visibly interrupts actual loadings, not another projectile. Until then, trade the retest and never the headline.
